question: How are meaningful chains in the graph selected?

evidence: While it is obvious that our embeddings can be used as features for new predictive models, it is also very easy to incorporate our learned Dolores embeddings into existing predictive models on knowledge graphs. The only requirement is that the model accepts as input, an embedding layer (for entities and relations). If a model fulfills this requirement (which a large number of neural models on knowledge graphs do), we can just use Dolores embeddings as a drop-in replacement. We just initialize the corresponding embedding layer with Dolores embeddings. In our evaluation below, we show how to improve several state-of-the-art models on various tasks simply by incorporating Dolores as a drop-in replacement to the original embedding layer.

evidence: Having generated a set of paths on knowledge graphs representing local contexts of entities and relations, we are now ready to utilize the machinery of language modeling using deep neural networks to learn Dolores embeddings.

After having estimated the parameters of the Dolores learner, we now extract the context-independent and context-dependent representations for each entity and relation and combine them to obtain Dolores embeddings. More specifically, Dolores embeddings are task specific combination of the context-dependent and context-independent representations learned by our learner. Note that our learner (which is an $L$ -layer Bi-Directional LSTM) computes a set of $2L + 1$ representations for each entity-relation pair which we denote by: $ R_t = [ x_t, \overrightarrow{h_{t,i}}, \overleftarrow{h_{t,i}} \mid i = 1, 2, \cdots , \textit {L} ], $

title: DOLORES: Deep Contextualized Knowledge Graph Embeddings
answer_short: By representing knowledge graphs as entity-relation chains and learning embeddings using deep neural models like Bi-Directional LSTMs.
answer_rationale: The selection of meaningful chains is based on representing knowledge graphs as entity-relation chains, which encode contextual usage. These chains are then used to learn embeddings via deep neural models, specifically Bi-Directional LSTMs, as described in the retrieved documents. This approach captures contextual cues and dependencies among entities and relations, enabling effective representation learning for downstream tasks.
